title: Dai Kenja — Doctrine of Overflow
revision: Draft 4 / Dai Kenja classification / forked tree

classification.applies_to: existing supported tags of every Dai Kenja jutsu

emphasis.primary: Overloaded Impact offense (Damage and Increase Damage Given)
emphasis.secondary: Decrease Damage Given (Chakra Overload / Chakra Cannon suppression)
emphasis.tertiary: Increase Damage Taken (Chakra Overload exposure; adverse on Overloaded Impact)
emphasis.rationale: The kit has six supported rows on three casts. Overloaded Impact carries the only Damage row (40 power at level 25) and the only Increase Damage Given row (30% self, Ninjutsu filter with no element, so it also admits every non-elemental hit; live only in the two rounds after the cast, so it never helps its own hit), making offense through that cast the primary in two separate forms: more power on the hit, or a stronger amplifier for the hits that follow; the bloodline's 15% passive multiplies under the same matching. Decrease Damage Given is the broadest tag (25% on Chakra Overload, 30% on the AOE Chakra Cannon, all stat types) and is secondary, so root B holds the heavier four-purchase builds by row weight (19–24 against 13–15 on root A) while root A holds the largest single-row flats (+6 Damage, +10 Increase Damage Given). Increase Damage Taken reaches Chakra Overload's 35% enemy exposure but also the adverse 25% self exposure on Overloaded Impact, so it is a small, explicitly accepted tertiary route; Chakra Cannon's pierce and Chakra Overload's pool-cost row are unsupported and untouched.

nodes.name: Brimming Cup
nodes.flavor: A sage's chakra fills the cup past its rim and keeps pouring.
nodes.coverage_note: Overloaded Impact self damage buff (30→33%); adds to Ninjutsu or non-elemental hits in the 2 rounds after each cast, never its own hit.

nodes.name: Chakra Surcharge
nodes.flavor: Every impact carries more than the body was meant to hold.
nodes.coverage_note: Overloaded Impact Damage only (40→43 power); single row, 60 AP, cooldown 6, single target at range 4. Chakra Cannon's pierce is unsupported.

nodes.name: Breaking Point
nodes.flavor: Push the overload one breath further than wisdom allows.
nodes.coverage_note: Overloaded Impact Damage (route 46 power) and its self buff (+2, 35% with Brimming Cup); the buff acts after the cast round, not on this hit

nodes.name: Flooded Meridians
nodes.flavor: Open every channel; let the current run where it will.
nodes.coverage_note: Overloaded Impact self damage buff only (33→36% with Brimming Cup); one row, Ninjutsu or non-elemental hits, 2 rounds after each cast.

nodes.name: Boundless Reservoir
nodes.flavor: There is no bottom to the well the Great Sage draws from.
nodes.coverage_note: Same self damage buff; route total +10 (30→40%, Ninjutsu or non-elemental hits, 2 rounds after each 60 AP cast, cooldown 6). No other row.

nodes.name: Sage's Rebuke
nodes.flavor: A word from the sage, and the enemy's chakra falters.
nodes.coverage_note: Chakra Overload (25→27%, enemies) and Chakra Cannon AOE (30→32%, any non-caster in circle) Decrease Damage Given, all stats, 2 rounds.

nodes.name: Smothered Current
nodes.flavor: Their flow is pinched to a trickle under the sage's hand.
nodes.coverage_note: Both Decrease Damage Given rows (+2 more: 29/34%); both debuffs stack on one target when both casts land; Cannon hits allies in its circle.

nodes.name: Edict of Silence
nodes.flavor: The sage speaks once; the enemy's power answers in a whisper.
nodes.coverage_note: Both suppression rows; route total +8 (Chakra Overload 33%, Chakra Cannon 38%; 71% stacked on one target). Cannon hits allies in its circle.

nodes.name: Cracked Vessel
nodes.flavor: Overload leaves fissures in the vessel, yours and theirs.
nodes.coverage_note: Chakra Overload enemy exposure (35→37%, Ninjutsu or non-elemental) AND adverse Overloaded Impact self exposure (25→27%, all damage).

nodes.name: Shattered Vessel
nodes.flavor: What is overfilled must break; the sage chooses when.
nodes.coverage_note: Enemy exposure route +5 (40%), self exposure 30% (adverse); both Decrease Damage Given rows +3 (route 30/35%); Cannon hits allies in circle.

examples.name: Breaking Point
examples.rationale: The +6 power route on the kit's only Damage row (Overloaded Impact 40→46), plus the self buff at 35% for the two rounds after the cast (never on the cast's own hit). Sage's Rebuke is the fourth purchase because it opens the control root (27/32% suppression) without touching the single Overloaded Impact rows again; Flooded Meridians (buff 38%) is the all-in alternative.

examples.name: Boundless Reservoir
examples.rationale: Overloaded Impact as a two-round amplifier: its self Increase Damage Given reaches 40% and adds 40% of the staged base to every Ninjutsu or non-elemental hit (normal jutsu, basic attacks, weapons) landed in the two rounds after the cast, never to the cast's own hit. Sage's Rebuke is the fourth purchase for a small suppression floor; Chakra Surcharge (43 power) is the offensive alternative.

examples.name: Edict of Silence
examples.rationale: Both Decrease Damage Given rows at the route maximum (Chakra Overload 33% on enemies, Chakra Cannon 38% on any non-caster in its AOE circle), adding to 71% on a target carrying both debuffs (casts in the same or consecutive rounds). Brimming Cup is the fourth purchase because it raises the self damage buff to 33% for no exposure cost; Cracked Vessel (+2 exposure, adverse) is the aggressive alternative.

examples.name: Shattered Vessel
examples.rationale: The overload gamble: Chakra Overload's enemy exposure (Ninjutsu or non-elemental damage, from every attacker) reaches 40% while Overloaded Impact's own self exposure (all damage) rises to 30%, and both suppression rows sit at +7 (32/37%). Smothered Current is the fourth purchase because it compounds the control casts; Brimming Cup (buff 33%) is the offensive alternative.

design_notes: Node split mirrors the kit's two sides. Brimming Cup (self) opens Overloaded Impact, forking into raw power (Chakra Surcharge → Breaking Point) and self buff (Flooded Meridians → Boundless Reservoir); Sage's Rebuke (enemy) opens Chakra Overload / Chakra Cannon, forking into suppression (Smothered Current → Edict of Silence) and exposure (Cracked Vessel → Shattered Vessel). Every Advanced Art is 3 BP deep. Boundless Reservoir and Edict are single-tag: their roots hold no second non-adverse tag.

Flats scale with coverage. Damage reaches one row (Overloaded Impact 40): +3/+3 (max 46 power), not the reference's +2/+3 over three rows. Increase Damage Given is one 30% self row: single-row ladder +3/+3/+4 (max 40%). Decrease Damage Given has two enemy rows that stack on one target (25%, 30%): +2/+2/+4 (max +8: 33/38%, 71% combined). Increase Damage Taken has one enemy and one adverse self row: one route at +2/+3 (max +5). Per-tag maxima are within guardrails and not jointly attainable.

Timing (SOURCE_MECHANICS §3b): Overloaded Impact's self buff is inert in its cast round (adjustDamageGiven skips new or cast-this-round effects, tags.ts 925; flags clear at round advance, util.ts 2567–2577), so it never touches its own hit, and cooldown 6 outlives it. In the two rounds after the cast the enhanced 33–40% adds that share of the staged base to every Ninjutsu or non-elemental hit (getEfficiencyRatio, tags.ts 3477–3510). Only the 15% bloodline passive multiplies.

Delivery and uptime: Overloaded Impact is 60 AP, cooldown 6, one single-target hit at range 4; its buff and self exposure live two rounds in every six. Chakra Overload is 40 AP single target, cooldown 6; Chakra Cannon a 60 AP AOE circle, cooldown 7. Both suppression debuffs sit on one target only when the casts land in the same or consecutive rounds (100 AP in all), so 71% is a ceiling. Ranked PvP and ranked sparring suppress tree effects. Nothing was simulated.

Fourth purchases: Burst takes Sage's Rebuke (27/32%) or Flooded Meridians (buff 38%); Amplifier, Sage's Rebuke or Chakra Surcharge (43 power); Suppression, Brimming Cup (buff 33%) or Cracked Vessel (exposure 37%, self 27%); Exposure, Smothered Current or Brimming Cup. Counting IDT as a gain, 13 of 14 full builds are non-dominated; IDT-neutral, 8 are and neither Vessel node appears, so Cracked Vessel earns its place as the Shattered Vessel gate. Adverse-aware dominance is tooling debt.

Tuning for review (OPEN_DECISIONS D11; values user-owned, unchanged): Shattered Vessel is the largest node (raw 6, row-weighted 12, 9 without the adverse row) against Edict of Silence 4/8, Breaking Point 5/5 and Boundless Reservoir 4/4; its full build scores 24 (19 without the adverse row; 4.0 per row vs Taiyo Kami's 3.4) while root A's score 13–15. Options: cut Shattered Vessel's DDG secondary to +2 (Exposure build 31/36%) or raise Edict of Silence to +5 (max DDG +9).
risks: Adverse row accepted (D11): IDT nodes also raise Overloaded Impact's self exposure (all damage; 27% Cracked Vessel, 30% Shattered Vessel) in the two rounds after each cast, atop the 5% IDT passive. Only the exposure route has the tag; the enemy row (Chakra Overload, Ninjutsu or non-elemental, 35→40%) needs its own 40 AP cast. Fallback: drop Shattered Vessel, keep Cracked Vessel as a leaf (max +2).

Ally hazard (Chakra Cannon#1; warning kept): Cannon is an OTHER_USER AOE circle with friendlyFire ALL, so an ally in the circle (never the caster) gets its two-round suppression at the enhanced 32–38% (actions.ts 1029–1060; process.ts 154–183); every DDG node raises it; positioning decides. Chakra Overload's DDG is ENEMIES-only; its ALL exposure row lands on an ally only if aimed at one.

Single-cast concentration: all five root-A nodes modify Overloaded Impact only (one 60 AP single-target cast, cooldown 6). The Burst route adds +6 power to one hit per cycle; the Amplifier route pays only on Ninjutsu or non-elemental hits landed in the two rounds after that cast, never on the cast's own hit.

Suppression stacking: Chakra Overload and Chakra Cannon apply separate two-round Decrease Damage Given debuffs; with BATTLE_TAG_STACKING on, every same-tag effect applies and the percentages add (process.ts 1109–1117), so one target's hits lose 55% of their staged base at baseline and 71% at the route maximum, more with an allied Dai Kenja. Flats were cut to +2/+2/+4 for this; not simulated.

Leakage: the self buff adds to every Ninjutsu or non-elemental hit the caster lands in the two rounds after its cast (normal jutsu, basic attacks, weapons); enemy-side suppression and exposure alter damage from allies and weapons too. Restricted casting scope does not restrict downstream benefit; stat filters on element-less rows are not binding (SOURCE_MECHANICS §3, getEfficiencyRatio).

Classification: no row in this kit carries an element, so the proposed 'Dai Kenja' label is a bloodline-keyed extension with no existing element to fall back on. Under the current resolver all 6 supported rows fall back to None, which would also reach every non-elemental row on any jutsu the player casts; the normal-jutsu collision is unverified. The tree is inert until that extension exists.

Unsupported rows: Chakra Cannon's pierce (58 at level 25) and Chakra Overload's increasepoolcost (100%) receive no bonus; because pierce is processed after the damage-modifier pass at the pin, the Amplifier and Exposure routes do not raise the pierce hit and the Suppression route does not reduce enemy pierce.

Rank context: Dai Kenja is a D-rank bloodline with B/C/A-rank jutsu, weaker unmodified than the A-rank reference; the tree equalises marginal opportunity, not final strength, and cross-bloodline comparison is deferred to the roster review. Normal-tree potency policy is not approved, so a combined stacking audit is required before implementation. No combat simulation was performed.

audit.revision: Draft 4 / Dai Kenja classification / forked tree
limits: Proposed potency classification behavior; not implemented or verified in the live engine.
All existing supported tags of Dai Kenja jutsu inherit Dai Kenja potency eligibility; original combat elements and target scopes stay intact.
Every matching row on a jutsu receives each matching modifier; repeated rows are counted separately.
Damage values are raw power, not final-damage percentages; percentage-valued tags are capped at 100.

Afterburn is an enemy debuff: for its existing duration, damage the target takes causes extra Afterburn damage at its percentage (60% cap per hit). It is not itself a damage instance; downstream instances were not simulated.
Unsupported tags (e.g. wound, shield, stun, pierce, absorb, poison, drain, summon) receive no bonuses.
No combat simulation. Budget and numerical non-dominance checks do not establish equal combat strength.
Main-tree effects, bloodline passives, equipment, AP, uptime and modifier delivery are outside this audit.
